chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), who said:

The private part (awrah) consists of two parts: the front (qubul) and the back (dubur). As for the back, it is covered by the two buttocks. So when you cover the penis and the two testicles, you have covered the private part. And he said in another report: As for the back, the two buttocks have covered it, and as for the front, cover it with your hand.

key_terms.الْعَوْرَةُ: Private parts; the area that must be covered

ai.seo_question: What are the two parts of the male awrah and how should they be covered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) to clarify the specific definition of 'awrah for men during ritual bathing, distinguishing between natural concealment by the buttocks and the need for active covering of the front. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of prayer and modesty in public spaces like bathhouses. It reflects the practical application of modesty principles derived from the Quran, emphasizing both physical coverage and spiritual awareness.
